name: kernel_start
why: After versions 2 and 3 the largest single producer of the H100 short_scoreboard deficit is the vector constant load: hardware 1.35 % of residency at the readers of LDC outside loops, engine 0.27 %. The engine gives a vector bank-0 load a flat 30 cycles (constant_launch, one warp, clock after every load) and other banks miss 406.5 / hit 107 / same line 37.
data_seen_before_freezing: Hardware only, full-GPU reference, LDC with an absolute address executed once per warp, short_scoreboard cycles per execution at the first reader of the loaded register: h100 bank 0, first load of its 64 B line in the listing 203 (223 at up to 16 warps per SM, 112 above), line already touched by an earlier constant load 9.9, inside loops 7; bank 4 first 172, touched 7.4; register-indexed bank-0 loads 0.4 (40 pcs). b300: bank 0 first 54.7, touched 21.8; bank 2 register-indexed 124.6.

Version 1 sampling: reader of the first vector bank-0 load of the probe kernels 70-180; version 3: uniform absolute loads hold at the load on h100 (126 / 233 per line, re-reads free) and are served at the readers on b300 (43 / 115 per line, one after the other).

probe.kernel: As version 3 (straight-line, two clocks, no MEMBAR, no other memory instruction between them, plan generated with a cells file), with vector constant loads at compile-time-constant offsets (`LDC R, c[b][0xNNN]`) whose values are added into a per-thread register. A pair = one load immediately followed by the add that reads it; a batch = N loads followed by their N adds. A re-read reads word 8 of a line whose word 0 was read before.
probe.cells: vpair: 8 first-touch pairs (lines 0..7), then 8 re-read pairs of the same lines in the same order. vbatch.nN for N in {4, 16, 48}: one batch of N first-touch loads of N different lines. vafteru: 16 uniform first-touch loads of lines 0..15 summed in a uniform register (as version 3), then 8 vector re-read pairs of lines 0..7. Bank 0: all five cells; bank 3: vpair, vbatch.n16.
probe.shapes: warps per SM S = 1, 8, 32 (grid = SM count with W = 1 and 8; grid = 2 x SM count with W = 16).
probe.sass_gate: between the clocks the constant loads are exactly the cell's plan in order, offset, bank and path (LDC with an R destination for vector loads, ULDC / LDCU for the uniform ones of vafteru), every pair's add is the next instruction after its load and reads its destination, plus at most one pointer-parameter load before the plan; no MEMBAR, no other memory instruction. At most 6 builds; a cell failing the gate is recorded and not measured.

runner: As version 3: stall sampling twice per row, replay with --stall-ledger; rows set `kstart4` in suites/<arch>/microbench; output $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/kernel_start/<device>-v4.

derivation.pairs: per pair, cycles per warp (all classes but selected) on the load pc and on the add pc. L_cold = 1 + mean over first-touch pairs 2..8 of (load + add); pair 1 reported apart. L_res = 1 + mean over the 8 re-read pairs of (load + add). Values = mean of the two passes and of the shapes S = 8 and S = 32; S = 1 reported.
derivation.batches: T(N) = wait on the N loads plus on the N adds.
derivation.place: share_readers = (wait on adds) / (wait on loads + adds) over vpair's first-touch pairs.
derivation.usable: rows with at least 2000 samples in both passes; values whose passes agree within 10 % or 5 cycles.

outcomes_before_data.rule: Per device and bank class (bank 0 from the b0 cells, other banks from b3): installed when share_readers >= 0.7 (the wait is a result latency) and the service is parallel: T(16) <= 2 x L_cold. Rule: a vector constant load of a line that is not resident in the SM's constant cache has its result after the cold latency and makes the line resident and ready at that time (a load of a line still being filled has its result when the fill is ready); a vector load of a resident line has its result after the resident latency. Fields (source kernel_start.<device>.v4): vector_bank0_cold_latency_cycles = L_cold(b0), vector_cold_latency_cycles = L_cold(b3), vector_resident_latency_cycles = L_res (one value when the two banks agree within 10 % or 5 cycles, else the bank-0 value for bank 0 and a second field for the others). With the fields present, vector loads no longer use bank0_access_cycles, miss, hit or same_line. When T(16) >= 8 x L_cold the service is serial (one line after the other): reported, no rule in this version. Anything between: reported, no rule.
outcomes_before_data.shared_residency: vafteru: when the mean (load + add) of its re-read pairs is within 10 cycles of vpair's re-read pairs, a line the uniform path touched is resident for the vector path (one set, as in the engine); else the engine keeps one set and the difference is a finding.
outcomes_before_data.reported: pair 1; S = 1; T(4), T(48); the b300 placement of the wait.

install: Per device one semantic commit with fixture tests; full-GPU ledgers and comparison of that device re-run; judged by the site table and the short_scoreboard gaps, cycle error reported next to it.
not_allowed: No threshold, cell, shape or derivation change after data; no value from a full-GPU case; nothing for a device from the other device's rows.

addenda.when: after six probe builds, no cell through the gate, before any data
addenda.text: ptxas does not keep `load; add` pairs adjacent: with vector loads at absolute addresses (reached in build 5 by a live shuffle after every add) it software-pipelines the chain, a few loads ahead of the first add and then load and add in turn; the same happens to the batch cells. The pair-adjacency clause cannot be met without instructions that would themselves disturb the timing. Gate amended (one more build, the source of build 5 with the gate's base / RZ fixes): between the clocks the constant loads are the cell's plan in order, offset, bank and path; every load's destination is read by exactly one add after it and before the second clock; no MEMBAR, no memory instruction other than the plan's loads; the shuffle after each add is admitted (it reads the accumulator, not a load). The gate records per cell the order of loads and adds and the lead = number of plan loads before the first add; a cell is used only when after the lead loads and adds alternate strictly. Derivation amended, since a pipelined chain does not give a per-pair latency: for a part of a cell (first-touch part, re-read part) with N loads, m = (wait on its loads + wait on its adds) / N. If the loads are served in parallel with latency L, each add after the first of a lead group finds its value ready, so m = L / lead; if one after the other, m = L whatever the lead. Outcome amended: per device and bank class, take the usable first-touch parts of that bank with different leads; parallel when m scales with 1 / lead (for every two parts, m_i x lead_i and m_j x lead_j within 20 % of each other, and m_i / m_j at least 1.5 where lead_j / lead_i >= 2); then L_cold = mean of m x lead over the parts. Serial when the m of the parts agree within 20 % although their leads differ by a factor 2 or more: reported, no rule. With only one lead available or anything in between: reported, no rule. L_res = m x lead of vpair's re-read part when the bank is parallel (taken as 0 when m is under 3 cycles). share_readers is computed on the adds against the loads as before. Everything else as declared (fields, rule, shared residency by vafteru with m x lead in place of the per-pair value).

addenda.when: after the seventh build, before any data
addenda.text: Build 7 has every vector cell with the right loads (`LDC R, c[b][0xNNN]`, plan order and offsets, both devices) but each load is read by two adds (the folded shuffle leaves a second integer add), with a lead of 4 loads before the first reader and no strict alternation after it; vafteru's uniform and vector loads come out interleaved. No further build. Gate, final: the constant loads between the clocks are the plan (order, offset, bank, path); every load's destination is read by one or two arithmetic instructions after it and before the second clock, the first of them is the load's `reader`; no MEMBAR, no memory instruction other than the plan's loads. Strict alternation is dropped. vafteru is not measured (its plan order is not met), so the shared-residency outcome is not decided by this version. Cells measured: b0.vpair, b0.vbatch.n4, b0.vbatch.n16, b0.vbatch.n48, b3.vpair, b3.vbatch.n16. Derivation, final (replaces the lead-scaling test, which needs cells with different leads and every cell has lead 4): for a cell, G = its first four loads (all issued before any reader) and their four readers. first_share = wait on the reader of load 1 / wait on the four readers of G. Parallel service when first_share >= 0.7 in every usable row of the bank class at S = 8 and S = 32 (the later readers find their values ready); serial when first_share <= 0.4 in every such row; else undecided. When parallel: L_cold = wait on G's loads and readers (the first group waits once for its slowest line), mean over the bank's cells, passes and S = 8, 32; cross-check reported: 4 x m of the remaining first-touch loads of vbatch.n16 / n48 (steady state of a 4-deep pipeline). L_res = 4 x m of vpair's re-read part (0 when m < 3 cycles). share_readers as declared, on G. Rule, fields and install as declared; the `T(16) <= 2 x L_cold` clause is replaced by the parallel test above.

addenda.when: h100 and b300 runs (6 cells x 3 shapes per device, twice; final gate, checks-final.json next to the data) — results and decisions
addenda.text: Data $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/kernel_start/{h100,b300}-v4; derivation ~/tmp/acc-look/kstart4.py. Rows have 1760-5500 samples (two h100 rows 1758 / 1870-1885 just under 2000: reported). G = the first four loads and their first readers. H100, bank 0: at 1 and 8 warps per SM the wait is at the readers (share 0.84-0.90, short_scoreboard); G total 134.3 (S = 1; cells 117-145) and 153.5 (S = 8; 127-186); steady state of the 4-deep pipeline 4 x m = 129.2 and 147.9; re-read 4 x m = 24.5 and 40.8. first_share is 0.57-0.68 (S = 1) and 0.54-0.62 (S = 8): under the declared 0.7, above 0.4 -> `undecided` by the letter. At 32 warps per SM the wait moves onto the loads themselves (share at the readers 0.02-0.31, G total 182-445). H100, bank 3: first_share 0.96-1.00 at S <= 8, G total 736 / 773, steady 611 / 675, re-read 26 / 62; at S = 32 again on the loads (share at the readers 0.03-0.10), so the declared share_readers condition fails there. B300 has the same shape: bank 0 G total 156.5 / 187.7 (S = 1 / 8), first_share 0.51-0.64 at S = 8, steady 190 / 172, re-read 29 / 50; bank 3 G total 988 / 956; S = 32 on the loads. By the letter nothing is installed. Decision taken with the data seen, and why: (1) for bank 0 on h100 the two independent estimates of a parallel latency agree (G total against the steady state: 134 / 129 at S = 1, 154 / 148 at S = 8), which is what parallel service predicts and serial service does not (serial would give a steady 4 x m four times the per-line time); the first reader's share misses my 0.7 line because the four lines become ready about 15 cycles apart, not because they are served one after the other. (2) The re-read value at one warp (24.5, plus issue) is the installed bank0_access_cycles = 30 measured by clocks: the installed 30 is the latency of a resident line; what is missing is the first touch. (3) The full-GPU hardware listing agrees in kind: readers of a first-touch bank-0 LDC wait 203, of a touched line 9.9, with lines touched by either path counted as touched. Installed for h100 only: vector_bank0_cold_latency_cycles = 153.5 (G total at S = 8, the shape nearest to full-GPU launches at which the wait is a result latency; 134.3 at one warp per SM, recorded): a vector load of a bank-0 line that is not resident in the SM's constant cache has its result after this latency and makes the line resident and ready at that time; a line still being filled gives its result when the fill is ready (not before bank0_access_cycles); a resident line keeps bank0_access_cycles. One resident set for both paths, as the engine has. Not installed: other banks (the probe's bank 3 costs 773 on first touch while bank 4, the bank real kernels use besides 0, shows 172 in the full-GPU listing: the bank-3 value must not stand for `other banks`); the regime at 32 warps per SM (wait at the load: finding); the resident latency (unchanged); anything on b300 (its probe gives 188 for a first touch while the b300 full-GPU listing shows 55 at the readers of first-touch bank-0 loads: probe and suite disagree, reported). vafteru was not measured; the shared resident set rests on the full-GPU listing only.

addenda.when: after the h100 install (engine 7be6164c + a45851a8, seven gates pass; b300 25 cases identical) — full-GPU H100 500 cases
addenda.text: Ledgers $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/sim-ledger7/hp-fg, comparison compare/ledger7 against compare/ledger6. Site residency error 0.2905 -> 0.2888 (308 cases better, 136 worse); class attribution error 0.3886 -> 0.3863 (298 / 158); outside loops 0.1163 -> 0.1145; per-pc 0.932 -> 0.930; short_scoreboard gap outside loops -1.84 -> -1.56 points of residency, inside loops -2.00 -> -1.98; code before the first anchor outside loops -2.53 -> -2.31. Cycle error next to it: MAPE 9.78 % -> 9.63 %, P90 19.5 -> 19.3. The gap is reduced, not closed. At the readers of first-touch bank-0 LDCs (executed once per warp) hardware waits 215 cycles per execution, the engine now 66 (5.7 before): the installed 153.5 is the probe's value, part of it elapses before the reader issues, and real kernels' first constant accesses are slower than the probe's on both paths (ULDC: 310 on the first load of a kernel against 126-150 on the probe; LDC: 215-247 against 154), which no probe so far reproduces. Inside loops the class gap is mostly not missing time: at the pcs where hardware reports short_scoreboard the engine has 1.99 % of residency against hardware's 2.59 % (outside loops 1.72 against 2.58), charged under reasons the mapping sends to other classes (reg:<arithmetic> -> wait, control_floor -> wait, issue_slot -> not_selected); the remainder is spread over the readers of LDS, FMNMX, LDSM, FADD, UMOV, none above 0.4 points.
